key_insight: Photovoltaics look energetically strong at the panel level, but their net energy and climate advantage drop sharply once firming, storage, backup, and grid reliability are included.
engineering_relevance: For grid and energy-system design, the critical question is not just how efficiently PV generates electricity, but whether the whole supply chain can deliver reliable power with positive net-energy surplus.
method: Includes component turnover, grids, storage, renewable overbuild, dispatchable backup, and fuel supply
Compares unfirmed renewables, battery balancing, hydrogen firming, and gas backup
evidence_signal: The abstract reports illustrative system-boundary results: unfirmed renewables retain EROI 10.7-16.0, but firmed options fall to 0.7-12.5 depending on storage and backup configuration, with GWP$_{100}$ intensities rising substantially under firming.
watch_item: The model is a benchmark accounting study, not a simulation or optimization of real systems, so actual deployments will likely have lower EROI and higher emissions than the idealized cases.
paper_title: Photovoltaics beyond the panel: system-level net energy under grid and firming constraints
